title: Interface lemmas at the AIR-constraint boundary close the whitepaper's main theorem
intent: Prove the whitepaper's main theorem — that trace data satisfying the AIR `Constraints` yields an agreeing execution — by composing one named interface lemma per constraint family (memory, range check, range-check builtin, instruction, step), each crossing the boundary from the `Constraints` record to the execution semantics (`Option.FnExtends`, `NextState`), so the glue never unfolds a constraint definition.

parent.name: execution_exists
parent.statement:
theorem execution_exists (char_ge : ringChar F ≥ 2 ^ 63) (inp : InputDataAux F)
    (c : Constraints inp) (hp : Hprob c) :
    ∃ mem : F → F,
      Option.FnExtends mem inp.memStar ∧
        (∀ i < inp.rcLen, ∃ (n : ℕ), n < 2 ^ 128 ∧ mem (inp.initialRcAddr + i) = (↑n : F)) ∧
          ∃ exec : Fin (inp.t + 1) → RegisterState F,
            (exec 0).pc = inp.pcI ∧
              (exec 0).ap = inp.apI ∧
                (exec 0).fp = inp.apI ∧
                  (exec (Fin.last inp.t)).pc = inp.pcF ∧
                    (exec (Fin.last inp.t)).ap = inp.apF ∧
                      ∀ i : Fin inp.t, NextState mem (exec i.castSucc) (exec i.succ)

children.name: mem_extends
children.statement: theorem mem_extends : Option.FnExtends (mem a' v') mem_star
children.closed_by: intro addr; cases' h : mem_star addr with val; exact mem_unique … (embed_mem ⟨addr, h'⟩)
children.note: Crosses the memory boundary: the constructed memory extends the input memory, closing the Option.FnExtends conjunct.

children.name: mem_pc
children.statement: theorem mem_pc (i : Fin T) : mem a' v' (pc i) = inst i
children.note: Address-family bridge: the reconstructed memory agrees with the pc address; the same lemma discharges the dst/op0/op1/rc address families.

children.name: mem_dst_addr
children.statement: theorem mem_dst_addr (i : Fin T) : mem a' v' (dst_addr i) = dst i
children.note: Term-mode wrapper: dst-address agreement reduces to mem_pc.

children.name: off_op0_in_range
children.statement: theorem off_op0_in_range (i : Fin T) : ∃ k : ℕ, k < 2 ^ 16 ∧ off_op0_tilde i = ↑k
children.closed_by: rcases rc_permutation …; use rc_min + a'NatOffset a' j; constructor
children.note: Offset range-check bridge: each offset is a field element below 2^16; the same lemma discharges op1/dst/rc16.

children.name: rc16_vals_in_range
children.statement: theorem rc16_vals_in_range (i : Fin T) : ∃ k : ℕ, k < 2 ^ 16 ∧ rc16_vals i = ↑k
children.note: Term-mode wrapper: rc16 range reduces to off_op0_in_range.

children.name: rc_val_checked
children.statement: theorem rc_val_checked (i : Fin rc_len) : ∃ k : ℕ, k < 2 ^ 128 ∧ rc_val i = ↑k
children.closed_by: rw [h_rc_value]; eight rcases of h_rc16_val; use …; norm_num and an arithmetic bound
children.note: Range-check-builtin bridge: eight 16-bit values pack into one 128-bit value, closing the range_checked conjunct.

children.name: inst_eq
children.statement:
theorem inst_eq :
  inst = (theInstruction h_bit offOp0_in_range offOp1_in_range offDst_in_range).toNat
children.note: Instruction bridge: the constraint instruction equals the reconstructed Instruction's toNat.

children.name: nextState_eq
children.statement: theorem nextState_eq : NextState mem ⟨pc, ap, fp⟩ ⟨next_pc, next_ap, next_fp⟩
children.note: Step bridge: closes the NextState conjunct from the pc/dst/op0/op1 agreements.

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem `Constraints c → ∃ witness, P₀ witness ∧ P₁ witness ∧ … ∧ Pₖ witness` whose conjuncts are separate obligations (here: memory extension, range-check coverage, and the per-step `NextState` relation) and whose hypotheses are packaged in a record or section-variable block so that each conjunct is already a named lemma `family-hypotheses → conjunct` in the same project.
applicability.use_when: each constraint family's hypotheses are bundled in one structure (or locale/section variables) whose fields are exactly the premises of one bridge lemma per family; the proof is then a straight-line assembly of `have := bridge_lemma …` calls, supplying the structure fields as arguments, and a final `use`/`exact` of the assembled facts.
applicability.avoid_when: a family must be partially unfolded to state the fact (the bridge lemma is not a clean consequence of one structure); the client needs the constraint internals rather than the abstract fact; or there is no shared boundary the children can cross independently, so the glue still has to reason inside the definitions.

consequences: The glue becomes a straight-line list of `have`s, but each bridge lemma takes a long argument list of the family's constraint fields (10-16 premises here), so a missing field surfaces as an elaboration error at the call site. The boundary lemmas must be stated at the right level: too coarse and a conjunct cannot be discharged, too fine and the glue still unfolds. Correctness now rests on each bridge lemma being true of its whole family, so a family split across several lemmas — the instruction family here needs `inst_eq` plus the four `tilde_eq` lemmas before `nextState_eq` — still has to be re-assembled in the glue.
